Connect to the Hansard database

Source: R/data-connection.R
db_connect.Rd

Opens the package's single read-only connection to the Australian Hansard DuckDB database. Any connection already open is closed first. The database file is never written to.

Usage

db_connect(path = NULL, sample = FALSE)

Arguments

path

Path to a hansard.duckdb file.

sample

If TRUE, use the small sample database bundled with the package.

Value

The DBI connection, invisibly.

Details

The file is chosen as follows. An explicit path or sample = TRUE is used as given (passing both is an error). With neither, the first of these that exists is opened:

  1. the file named by the AUSPARL_DB environment variable;

  2. the copy installed by db_download() in the user data directory, for the database version this release of ausparl pins;

  3. the full database opened earlier in this R session (never the bundled sample);

  4. hansard.duckdb in the working directory, then in its dataset/ folder, as db_download(dir = ".") and db_download(dir = "dataset") leave it.

A message says which file was opened in cases 2 to 4. db_connect() never downloads anything itself.

On connect the DuckDB full-text-search extension (fts) is loaded. If it is not installed yet, it is installed once into tools::R_user_dir("ausparl", "cache"), which needs network access. Installation never happens during tests or R CMD check, and is switched off with options(ausparl.auto_install_fts = FALSE). Without fts every other function works; full-text search reports how to install it.

DuckDB's memory use is capped by the ausparl.memory_limit option, default "3GB". Accepted values are a size with a unit, such as "500MB", "1.5GB" or "2GiB"; anything else is an error and the current connection stays open. The cap bounds query execution itself, not just the results returned to R: a large query spills to disk rather than exceeding it, so expect peak R process memory of roughly the cap plus twice the result. Spill files go to an ausparl-duckdb directory under tempdir(), never beside the database file, and are removed when the R session ends. Change the option, then call db_connect() again to apply it.

See also

db_disconnect(), db_info(), db_download()

Examples

db_connect(sample = TRUE)
db_info()
#> # A tibble: 1 × 8
#>   schema_version built_at            builder_version path          fts_available
#>   <chr>          <dttm>              <chr>           <chr>         <lgl>        
#> 1 7.0.0          2026-11-23 13:40:39 0.0.0.9000      /home/runner… TRUE         
#> # ℹ 3 more variables: n_sittings <int>, n_actions <int>, n_members <int>
db_disconnect()
